extracted.intended_audience: owners/operators of electric utilities and independent power producers, permitting authorities, state/tribal regulators, and other stakeholders in CCR rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory requirements for implementation and evaluation of the EPA's proposed amendments to 40 CFR part 257 (disposal of coal combustion residuals), including applicability, definitions, reporting/recordkeeping, technical standards, and required analyses under statutory and Executive Order reviews (e.g., EJ, children's health, energy).

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Order 12866 significant regulatory action review
rubrics_metrics.description: This action is a “significant regulatory action” under section 3(f)(1) of Executive Order 12866, as amended by Executive Order 14094; accordingly, the EPA submitted this action to the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) for review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any changes made in response to recommendations received as part of Executive Order 12866 review have been documented in the docket. EPA prepared an analysis of the potential costs and benefits associated with this action (Regulatory Impact Analysis), which is available in the docket and briefly summarized in Unit V.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paperwork Reduction Act (PRA) — ICR submission and approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Information collection activities in this rule will be submitted for approval to OMB under the PRA; EPA submitted the proposed rule ICR to OMB on March 25, 2024, triggering a 30-day public comment period for the proposed information collection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final ICR will not be enforceable until OMB approves it. EPA assigned the ICR EPA ICR number 2761.01 and is requesting a temporary OMB control number pending approval; EPA intends to merge this rulemaking collection into existing ICR 2050-0223 upon approval. The final rule requires legacy CCR surface impoundments to comply with existing reporting and recordkeeping requirements, and to submit an applicability report unique to this universe of units. Respondents/affected entities, obligation to respond (mandatory recordkeeping/notification/posting under RCRA sections cited), estimated number of respondents (2,083), frequency (one-time and annually), total estimated burden (172,909 hours/year), and total estimated cost ($11.2 million/year) are summarized; when OMB approves the ICR, EPA will announce approval in the Federal Register and publish an amendment to 40 CFR part 9 to display the OMB control number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Flexibility Act (RFA) certification and analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA certifies this action will not have a significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities under the RFA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA identified 175 small entities subject to the final rule and estimates average annual cost to a small entity of approximately $0.31 million. EPA identified 15 small entities owning legacy CCR impoundments and estimates these 15 may incur $52.1 million in annual costs; EPA determined five small entities may experience an impact greater than 3% of annual revenues. Details are presented in the Regulatory Impact Analysis in the docket.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unfunded Mandates Reform Act (UMRA) analysis and consultation
rubrics_metrics.description: This action contains a Federal mandate under UMRA that may result in expenditures of $100 million or more for State, local and Tribal governments, or the private sector in any one year; accordingly EPA prepared the written statement required under section 202 of UMRA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA estimated the universe affected (legacy CCR impoundments, CCRMU, OAFUs, and landfills) and summarized that the final rule merely extends provisions of the 2015 CCR final rule to additional classes of facilities. EPA followed intergovernmental consultation provisions (section 204) and small government consultation per its interim plan (section 203) when preparing the 2015 rule; consistent with section 205 EPA identified and considered reasonable regulatory alternatives and adopted the least-costly approach (modified “D Prime”). The action is not subject to section 203 (no regulatory requirements that might significantly or uniquely affect small governments) based on cost thresholds described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Order 13132 Federalism determination
rubrics_metrics.description: This action does not have Federalism implications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA concludes the action will not have substantial direct effects on States, the relationship between the national government and the States, or the distribution of power and responsibilities among levels of government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Order 13175 Tribal consultation and implications
rubrics_metrics.description: This action does not have Tribal implications as specified in Executive Order 13175.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA identified three coal-fired electric utility plants (in operation as of 2012) located on Tribal lands; to the extent these plants contain CCRMU subject to the rule, impacts are limited to document review and walking the site, not substantial direct costs. Thus EO 13175 does not apply to this action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Order 13045 Protection of Children analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Because this is a significant regulatory action and EPA believes the environmental health or safety risks addressed may have a disproportionate effect on children, the action is subject to EO 13045 and EPA's Policy on Children's Health applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA identified seven age cohorts (infants <1 yr; 1 to <2 yr; 2 to <3 yr; 3 to <6 yr; 6 to <11 yr; 11 to <16 yr; 16 to <21 yr) and used exposure factors for each cohort to calculate cancer and non-cancer risk results in both screening and probabilistic analyses. Screening risks exceeded human health criteria for certain pathways (air, soil, food from fugitive dust and runoff); 90th percentile child risks exceeded criteria for groundwater-to-drinking-water under full probabilistic analysis. EPA concludes closure, groundwater monitoring, and corrective action required by the rule will reduce risks and be protective of children's health.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Order 13211 energy effects assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: This action is not a “significant energy action” under EO 13211 because it is not likely to have a significant adverse effect on the supply, distribution, or use of energy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the rule mainly pertains to inactive units and regulated facilities, EPA concluded no direct effect on energy production. Indirect electricity price effects were estimated by comparing expected rule costs to prior IPM runs (2015 CCR, 2015 ELG, 2019 ELG), and extrapolating an estimated national electricity price effect between 0.060% and 0.156%—below the 1% threshold, so no significant adverse energy effects are expected. Full energy impacts analysis is in the RIA.

rubrics_metrics.name: National Technology Transfer and Advancement Act (NTTAA) — use of voluntary consensus standards
rubrics_metrics.description: This rulemaking involves technical standards and EPA decided to use existing voluntary consensus standards relied on by the CCR regulations (e.g., ASTM, EPA SW-846 test methods).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically: (1) §257.70 liner design criteria for new CCR landfills and lateral expansions include ASTM and SW-846 methods; (2) §257.71 liner design criteria for existing CCR surface impoundments include ASTM and SW-846; (3) §257.72 liner design criteria for new CCR surface impoundments and expansions include ASTM and SW-846; (4) §257.73 structural stability standards for new and existing surface impoundments rely on ASTM D 698 and 1557 for embankment compaction. This rule expands §257.73 to facilities with legacy CCR surface impoundments and does not adopt additional technical standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Order 12898 Environmental Justice (EJ) analysis requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA conducted a demographic screening analysis for all facilities subject to the rule to determine the composition of populations within one and three miles, focusing on metrics indicating minority status, poverty, education, and linguistic isolation, and expanded the analysis to include health and social indicators relevant to the rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA looked at percentages of populations identified as minority/people of color, households below Federal poverty level, population with less than high school education (25+), and linguistic isolation for radii of one and three miles. EPA also included eight baseline indicators from CDC Environmental Justice Index (EJI) and EPA's EJScreen: CDC EJI indicators (lack of internet access, prevalence of disabilities, cancer, poor mental health, high blood pressure, asthma, diabetes) and EJScreen indicators (PM2.5 concentrations and low life expectancy). For each indicator, EPA identified communities falling in the highest 40% (top two quintiles) nationwide. The analysis found more than half of roughly 182 sites are located in areas with EJ concerns. EPA concluded the rule will likely reduce disproportionate and adverse effects, improve environmental quality, require facilities to publish contamination/remediation info on public websites, and thus improve access to information for affected communities. EPA also noted lack of internet access as a barrier and its implications for information access requirements of the rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Congressional Review Act (CRA) compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: This action is subject to the Congressional Review Act and EPA will submit a rule report to each House of Congress and to the Comptroller General of the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This action meets the criteria set forth in 5 U.S.C. 804(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory nature of recordkeeping, notification, and posting under RCRA
rubrics_metrics.description: Recordkeeping, notification, and posting are mandatory as part of the minimum national criteria promulgated under Sections 1008(a), 2002(a), 4004, and 4005(a) and (d) of RCRA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondents include inactive electric utility plants with inactive CCR surface impoundments (legacy CCR surface impoundments), electric utility plants with CCRMU, electric utility plants with OAFUs, and electric utility plants with landfills already subject to regulation under the 2015 final CCR rule but which have waste in contact with groundwater. The final rule requires legacy CCR surface impoundments to comply with reporting/recordkeeping requirements already in place for regulated CCR units and to submit an applicability report providing essential site characteristic and contact information.

rubrics_metrics.name: §257.50 Scope and applicability (expanded applicability criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: Revisions to §257.50 clarify the scope: (c) applies to inactive CCR surface impoundments at active electric utilities or independent power producers regardless of how electricity is produced; (d)(1) applies to CCR management units containing 1,000 tons or greater of CCR located at active facilities or facilities with a legacy CCR surface impoundment; (d)(2) CCRMU containing >=1 ton and <1,000 tons are subject only to facility evaluation report requirements until a permitting authority determines regulation is warranted; (e) applies to electric utilities or independent power producers that ceased producing electricity prior to Oct 19, 2015 and have a legacy CCR surface impoundment onsite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These applicability thresholds determine which units are regulated initially and which are subject only to facility evaluation pending permitting authority determination; owners/operators must ascertain applicability per these provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: §257.52 Applicability of other regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Compliance with the requirements of subpart D does not affect the need for the owner or operator of a CCR unit to comply with all other applicable federal, state, tribal, or local laws or other requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any CCR unit continues to be subject to the requirements in §§257.3-1, 257.3-2, and 257.3-3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions that establish scope and responsibilities (§257.53)
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensive revisions and additions to definitions (e.g., active facility; closed prior to Oct 19, 2015; CCR landfill; CCR management unit; CCR surface impoundment; CCR unit; contains both CCR and liquids; critical infrastructure; inactive CCR landfill; inactive CCR surface impoundment; inactive facility; infiltration; legacy CCR surface impoundment; liquids; operator; owner; regulated CCR unit; State Director; technically feasible; technically infeasible).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These definitions determine which sites and activities are covered and the duties of owners/operators. Example definitions provided include: 'CCR management unit' = any area of land on which any noncontainerized accumulation of CCR is received, placed, or managed that is not a regulated CCR unit; 'legacy CCR surface impoundment' = CCR surface impoundment that no longer receives CCR but contained both CCR and liquids on or after Oct 19, 2015 and is located at an inactive electric utility; 'contains both CCR and liquids' except as demonstrated under §257.102(d)(2)(i). 'Technically feasible' = possible to do in a way that would likely be successful; 'technically infeasible' = not possible to do in a way that would likely be successful.

rubrics_metrics.name: §257.61 Wetlands siting prohibition (with demonstration exceptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: New CCR landfills, existing and new CCR surface impoundments, and all lateral expansions of CCR units must not be located in wetlands (as defined in §230.41(a)), unless the owner or operator demonstrates by specified dates that the unit meets the requirements of paragraphs (a)(1) through (5) of the section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owners/operators wishing to site or expand in wetlands must satisfy the demonstration requirements and meet any deadlines specified in paragraph (c).

rubrics_metrics.name: §257.73 Structural integrity criteria applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirements of paragraphs (a)(1) through (4) of §257.73 apply to all existing CCR surface impoundments and legacy CCR surface impoundments, except for incised CCR surface impoundments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA revised the introductory text to make structural stability requirements explicitly applicable to legacy impoundments; owners/operators must meet the structural integrity criteria unless their impoundment is classified as incised.

rubrics_metrics.name: §257.75 Requirements for identifying CCR management units (facility evaluation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators of active facilities or facilities with a legacy CCR surface impoundment must conduct a facility evaluation to identify all CCR management units at the facility in accordance with paragraphs (c) through (e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At minimum, the presence or absence of CCR management units must be confirmed and documented through a thorough evaluation of reasonably and readily available records that contain information needed to prepare the Facility Evaluation Reports Part 1 and Part 2 required by paragraphs (c) and (d). The facility evaluation must also include a physical inspection of the facility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory rulemaking factor: selection without consideration of cost under RCRA
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA establishes the requirements under RCRA sections 1008(a)(3) and 4004(a) without taking cost into account; although EPA prepared a benefit-cost analysis, it did not rely on that analysis in selecting the proposed alternative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA states it designed the proposal based on statutory factors and court precedent; after considering unquantified and distributional effects, EPA believes health and welfare gains justify the rule's costs, but the statutory selection of requirements did not depend on cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information availability and internet-access consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rule requires that facilities make information about their contamination and remediation actions available on public websites to provide interested members of the public, including communities with EJ concerns, improved access to information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA identified lack of internet access in surrounding communities as a barrier to receiving required information; lack of internet access often associates with poverty but is distinct and widespread, and EPA considers it in assessing how information requirements affect communities.
